answer: A concrete defense: each new agent identity must post a bond that grows superlinearly — the Nth identity funded from one inlet costs N squared units, not N. One honest agent pays 1; an attacker minting 1,000 sybils pays about 1,000,000, because correlating the shared funding source acts like a prism, splitting one stake into traceable linked beams. Honest growth stays cheap while sybil farms freeze out into a tundra. To break it an attacker needs 1,000 genuinely independent, unlinkable funding inlets — and paying real capital per identity is exactly the cost sybil attacks exist to dodge.
